method: scripts/ib-research/claim-check.js: the passage is copied verbatim from the live source text at the pinned revision; VERIFIED = every claim number in one sentence that shares >= 50% of the claim's content words

records.claim: Earth currently has an axial tilt of about 23.44°.
records.passage: Earth currently has an axial tilt of about 23.44°.

records.claim: Mars's obliquity is quite variable over millions of years; it varies as much as 0° to 60° depending on perturbations of the planets.
records.passage: Mars's obliquity is quite variable over millions of years and may be in a chaotic state; it varies as much as 0° to 60° over some millions of years, depending on perturbations of the planets.

records.claim: Nutation adds short-period oscillations of about 9.2 arcseconds over about 18.6 years.
records.passage: Periodic motions of the Moon and of Earth in its orbit cause much smaller (9.2 arcseconds) short-period (about 18.6 years) oscillations of the rotation axis of Earth, known as nutation, which add a periodic component to Earth's obliquity.

records.claim: Simulations in 2011 indicated that even without the Moon, Earth's obliquity might vary only by about 20–25°.
records.passage: However, more recent numerical simulations made in 2011 indicated that even in the absence of the Moon, Earth's obliquity might not be quite so unstable; varying only by about 20–25°.

narration.text: Double Earth's tilt, and seasons turn extreme.
Today the axis leans about 23.44 degrees.
That tilt, not distance from the Sun, makes seasons.
Double it, and months of polar night creep toward mid-latitudes.
Summers would get hotter, winters darker and longer.
Mars shows how wild it gets: its tilt swings between 0 and 60 degrees.
Earth's own tilt barely wobbles today, only by arcseconds.
So a stable tilt is one reason seasons are survivable.
